To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a discrete time single loop second order 5-bit delta sigma modulator is implemented using a novel dynamic amplifier based integrator and inter-stage passive sampling method in 65 nm CMOS technology, and that the proposed modulator achieves 91.2 db peak SNDR and 94 μW power consumption from a 1 V supply.

a 2nd order single loop 5-bit Δ Σ ADC with a dynamic amplifier based integrator and passive sampling method achieves 91.2-dB peak SNDR in the 24-kHz band, consumes only 94 μW from 1-V supply and achieves a FoM of 66.1 fJ/conv.
the proposed modulator achieves high SNDR and high FOM with a small chip area.

the design of high performance low power ΔΣ modulators. 1.1.

the design of a 91.2-dB SNDR 66 fJ/conv. 24-kHz dynamic amplifier based ΔΣ modulator in 65 nm CMOS is presented.
the design is very competitive in terms of power efficiency and area efficiency.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a high SNDR, low power, and small area modulator is achieved by the proposed dynamic amplifier based integrator and passive inter-stage sampling.
a 91.2dBSNR 66.2 fJ/conv. ΔΣ modulator can be achieved with a 0.11 mm2 core area.
we have designed a power efficient 5th order modulator for digital audio and sensors applications with a FOM of only 66.2 fJ/conv.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed integrator can be used to implement high-order and high-resolution ΔΣ modulators with a low supply voltage and a small area.
we can achieve a high SNDR in a small area and low power consumption by using the proposed integrator and the 3-D capacitances.
the dynamic amplifier based integrator can save the static current consumption and the passive inter-stage sampling is effective to save the active buffer.
